title: Advanced Delegation and Property Design
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of advanced delegation and property design using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates advanced delegation and property design.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Advanced Delegation and Property Design** as part of **Advanced Kotlin Language Features**. Classes group state and behavior; primary constructors and properties keep ordinary domain models concise, while initialization order still matters. Use the subtopics—Custom Delegate Implementations, Delegate Operator Conventions, Delegation and API Boundaries—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

items.text: Delegation and API Boundaries crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.
